subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should run-scoped tool bindings become a supported plugin-facing API, or should the browser copilot retain that authority through a browser-specific internal owner seam?
rationale: The change exposes a new generic binding object to plugin tool factories, which sets a durable authorization and compatibility boundary that cannot be selected safely by automated repair.

options.title: Define a supported binding contract
options.body: Document and version a narrow plugin-facing run-binding API, migrate internal consumers to it, and add compatibility coverage.

options.title: Keep bindings browser-owned
options.body: Remove the generic plugin context field and pass the capability through a browser-specific internal integration seam.

options.title: Pause the feature boundary
options.body: Defer this PR until maintainers decide the permanent plugin authorization model for run-bound tools.

recommendation.title: Define a supported binding contract
recommendation.body: Document and version a narrow plugin-facing run-binding API, migrate internal consumers to it, and add compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation series spans the browser, Gateway, pairing, and plugin-context boundary where this API direction must be resolved.
